::: solve S-6e8a43cc
type: cloze
question: ____ is the kinetic energy associated with the random motion of atoms and molecules.
context: [p.2] Energy can be converted from one form to another, but it is never created or destroyed. This principle is called the law of conservation of energy. ¶ The atoms and molecules in any sample of matter are in constant random motion. Thermal energy is the kinetic energy associated with the random motion of these particles. A cup of hot tea has more thermal energy than the same cup of tea after it has cooled, because its molecules move faster on average. ¶ PE max
answer: Thermal energy
evidence: Thermal energy is the kinetic energy associated with the random motion of these particles
:::

::: solve S-a0dddd9d
type: mcq
question: Which statement correctly tells kinetic energy apart from potential energy?
option A: Kinetic energy comes from motion; potential energy comes from position, composition, or condition.
option B: Kinetic energy is stored in batteries; potential energy belongs to moving objects.
option C: Both kinds of energy depend only on an object's speed.
option D: Potential energy can supply heat or do work, but kinetic energy cannot.
context: [p.1] Kinetic energy is the energy that an object possesses because of its motion. A rolling ball, a flowing river, and a vibrating molecule all have kinetic energy. The kinetic energy of an object depends on both its mass and its speed: ¶ KE = ½mv² (1.1) … [p.2] Potential energy is the energy that an object possesses because of its position, composition, or condition. A ball held above the ground has gravitational potential energy, and a battery stores chemical potential energy in the arrangement of its atoms. ¶ Energy can be converted from one form to another, but it is never created or destroyed. This principle is called the law of conservation of energy.
answer: A
only-one-correct: yes
evidence: Kinetic energy is the energy that an object possesses because of its motion
:::

::: solve S-7324e950
type: numeric
question: A 2.00 kg cart moves at 3.00 m/s. What is its kinetic energy in joules?
context: [p.1] Kinetic energy is the energy that an object possesses because of its motion. A rolling ball, a flowing river, and a vibrating molecule all have kinetic energy. The kinetic energy of an object depends on both its mass and its speed: ¶ KE = ½mv² (1.1)
answer: 9.00[J]
evidence: KE = ½mv² (1.1)
calc: KE = 1/2 * 2.00[kg] * (3.00[m/s])^2 => 9.00[J]
:::

::: solve S-f40afb80
type: mcq
question: Why do chemists often report energies in kilojoules rather than joules?
option A: A joule is a small amount of energy.
option B: The joule is not an SI unit.
option C: Food labels are required to use kilojoules.
option D: A kilojoule is smaller than a joule.
context: [p.3] • Convert between joules and calories ¶ The SI unit of energy is the joule (J). One joule is the kinetic energy of a 2-kg object moving at a speed of 1 meter per second. A joule is a small amount of energy, so chemists often report energies in kilojoules (kJ); 1 kJ = 1000 J.
answer: A
only-one-correct: yes
evidence: A joule is a small amount of energy
:::
